children: Shares of State Bank of India (SBI) opened 1% lower on Friday, September 11, while Vodafone Idea shares were trading 2% higher.

The moves come after CNBC-TV18 reported on Thursday that an SBI-led consortium of lenders is at an advanced stage of evaluating Vodafone Idea's funding proposal, after the telecom operator submitted a detailed plan outlining its borrowing requirement and proposed use of funds.
Sources told CNBC-TV18 that the proposal covers around ₹35,000 crore, including ₹25,000 crore in funded facilities and ₹10,000 crore in non-funded facilities.

SBI is expected to lead the consortium, with most large lenders likely to participate. However, each lender's board will need to approve its individual share of the proposed funding before the consortium can give final approval.
Lenders are also seeking repayment guarantees in the event of a default, according to sources. Even after formal approvals, it could take some time for the funds to be disbursed.
Vodafone Idea plans to use part of the proposed funding to strengthen its network and improve its competitive position, according to the proposal.
The company has been seeking fresh debt to shore up its finances. CNBC-TV18 had reported in May that Vodafone Idea was in talks with lenders and that SBI was likely to lead the consortium.
Jefferies sees Vodafone Idea as 'high-beta turnaround opportunity'
Separately, brokerage firm Jefferies initiated coverage on Vodafone Idea on Thursday, September 10, calling it a "high-beta turnaround opportunity" in the Indian telecom sector.
Jefferies has assigned a price target of ₹20 to the stock. The target is also the highest among the 22 analysts covering the stock, according to the brokerage.
The ₹20 target comes with only the fourth 'Buy' recommendation on Vodafone Idea, while a majority of analysts covering the stock have a 'Sell' rating.

Jefferies expects subscriber stabilisation at Vodafone Idea to support revenue growth at a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) of 11% between financial year 2026 and financial year 2029. Combined with strong operating leverage, this is expected to drive a 25% CAGR in cash EBITDA over the same period and a sharp improvement in return on invested capital (RoIC) through financial year 2031.

Vodafone Idea is expected to deliver incremental EBITDA margins of around 50% between financial year 2026 and financial year 2029, below the 60%-plus margins typically seen at telecom companies, given the accelerated network rollout during this period, Jefferies said.
The brokerage expects margins to rise above 60% after financial year 2030, once the network rollout normalises.

Jefferies estimates that raising ₹25,000 crore in debt would be sufficient for Vodafone Idea to navigate the next couple of years. However, the company would need a fresh equity infusion of ₹16,000 crore in financial year 2030.

This would also trigger the conversion of spectrum liabilities worth ₹15,300 crore into equity by the government. Jefferies believes the combined measures should be sufficient to cover the company's cash flow shortfall between financial year 2030 and financial year 2034.

Vodafone Idea has already raised ₹44,700 crore through equity since 2019. Jefferies believes raising an additional ₹16,000 crore should not be difficult, given improving operating cash flows and continued government support.

title: Vodafone Idea shares gain as SBI-led consortium evaluates ₹35,000 crore funding proposal
